note: Lifted legacy model. An alarm is a catch-all, bundling an event, an undesirable state, a fixed severity and a static probable-cause, all hard-coded at emission. ref=null marks a native concept with no shared category.

concepts.label: managed-object
concepts.gloss: a managed element the fault manager watches
concepts.example: router R7; the BGP session to AS64500

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: a syslog message or SNMP trap: something happened on a resource at a moment
concepts.example: a BGP state-change trap on the session at t0

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: an emitted alarm: an undesirable condition (a state) on a resource that also implies a fault occurrence, carrying a fixed severity and a probable cause; the catch-all that bundles what NMOP separates
concepts.example: a MAJOR 'session-down' alarm on the BGP session to AS64500

concepts.label: severity
concepts.gloss: the fixed severity label assigned at emission: critical, major, minor or warning - static, not recomputed from context

concepts.label: probable-cause
concepts.gloss: a static probable-cause code from the X.733 dictionary, fixed at emission - not derived by correlating events

concepts.label: clear
concepts.gloss: a notification that a previously raised alarm condition has cleared
